function: above_phy: the DDQN agent only raises or lowers the spectrum price one level (p. 7, Eq. 11) to maximize leasing revenue, a market decision above the physical layer.
notes: Identity checked: PDF is the arXiv version of 'Privacy-Aware Spectrum Pricing and Power Control Optimization for LEO Satellite Internet-of-Things' (p. 1), matching the DOI. Why above_phy: the action of the DDQN agent is the 'price level decision' (p. 7, Eq. 11), its state is price and utility (Eq. 10) and its reward is revenue (Eq. 12). Blockchain-driven FL aggregates the pricing models digitally (pp. 8-9, Algorithm 2), not over the air. The uplink power-control level is adjusted by satellite operators under the reputation rule (p. 8: 'adjust the power control level'), so it is not an action of the learned agent. No link metric is evaluated: results are reward, price and revenue (pp. 11-14, Figs. 7-10). Borderline points for the reviewer: (1) Algorithm 1 (p. 7), titled 'Local Pricing and Power Controlling', says in line 12 'change the price of the spectrum or the control level of power', and the title and abstract name power control, but the formal MDP has no power action. (2) The protocol counts learned resource allocation in satellite links as physical layer; I read the pricing of idle spectrum as a market decision, not an allocation of power, bandwidth or beams. If the reviewer reads either point the other way, the work falls in area 6 (single-antenna links are admitted) with q1=0 (custom LEO simulator, p. 12), q2=0, q3=0 (the only learned baseline is plain DDQN, a variant of the proposed method, Fig. 10, pp. 13-14), q4=1 (Section IV-E, p. 10: O(KE sum L_i L_i+1)), q5=0.
